report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Verify that an evaluation would score the candidate's own daedalus checkout by probing the candidate's interpreter, and void the evaluation on any failure.

symbols.name: PROBE_SOURCE
symbols.note: Python source string run in the candidate's interpreter; reports argv0, executable, path0, daedalus file and path, or import error, as JSON on stdout.

symbols.name: ProvenanceCheck
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding ok, root, resolved, reason, raw; as_error() formats an evaluation-void message that never says 'candidate'.

symbols.name: ProvenanceCheck.as_error
symbols.note: Returns a string stating the evaluation is void, not a candidate failure.

symbols.name: _under
symbols.note: Returns True if the child path resolves inside the parent directory; False on empty child or resolve/relative_to errors.

symbols.name: check_import_provenance
symbols.note: Runs the probe in the candidate's cwd with the given or current executable, parses JSON, and returns a ProvenanceCheck; fail-closed on any error.

claims.text: The runner now uses sys.executable -m pytest with cwd set to the worktree, which puts the worktree on sys.path[0]
claims.why: The runner invocation is not in this file; this chunk cannot observe it.

claims.text: This module exists because that is a MECHANISM, not a VERIFICATION
claims.why: The module performs a runtime probe and voids the evaluation on failure rather than relying on import-order reasoning.

claims.text: It stops holding if PYTHONPATH is set in the environment the evaluator inherits
claims.why: The probe inherits the environment, but this chunk does not test or manipulate PYTHONPATH; the claim is about a scenario not exercised here.

claims.text: a candidate worktree has no daedalus/ directory at all
claims.why: If no daedalus directory exists, the probe will report an import_error or resolve outside the tree, and check_import_provenance returns ok=False.

claims.text: a future refactor changes how the editable install registers itself
claims.why: No editable-install code is present in this chunk; the claim concerns future changes outside this file.

claims.text: somebody 'simplifies' the invocation back to bare pytest
claims.why: The test invocation is not in this file; this chunk cannot observe it.

claims.text: In every one of those cases the failure is the WORST shape available: the tests pass, the score is high, and it describes the wrong tree
claims.why: The claim describes outcomes of scenarios not exercised in this chunk; the module only detects resolution outside the tree.

claims.text: a failed check voids the EVALUATION rather than scoring the candidate
claims.why: as_error() explicitly says 'EVALUATION VOID (not a candidate failure)', and check_import_provenance returns ok=False without producing a score.

claims.text: Cheap: one interpreter start, ~0.3 s
claims.why: No timing measurement exists in this chunk; the performance claim is not verifiable here.

claims.text: Run in the CANDIDATE's interpreter, cwd and environment -- not here
claims.why: check_import_provenance invokes [exe, '-c', PROBE_SOURCE] with cwd=str(base), so the probe runs in the candidate's interpreter and directory.

claims.text: Reports rather than asserts, so the caller decides
claims.why: The probe prints JSON and exits 0 on import failure; only check_import_provenance interprets the output into ok=False.

claims.text: A probe that exited non-zero on mismatch would be indistinguishable from a probe that failed to start
claims.why: The probe never exits non-zero on a resolution mismatch; it reports via JSON, so a non-zero return always indicates a start/run failure.

claims.text: Whether an evaluation in root would score the code in root
claims.why: The class holds ok, root, resolved, and reason; ok=True only when resolved is inside root.

claims.text: The message an evaluator should record when this fails
claims.why: as_error() returns a string describing the evaluation as void with the reason and resolution.

claims.text: Deliberately says 'evaluation' and never 'candidate'
claims.why: The returned string begins 'EVALUATION VOID (not a candidate failure)' and contains no word 'candidate'.

claims.text: FAIL-CLOSED in every direction
claims.why: Every failure mode -- probe start error, non-zero return, unparseable output, import error, resolution outside tree -- returns ok=False.

claims.text: A probe that will not start, times out, returns unparseable output, or cannot import daedalus at all reports ok=False
claims.why: Lines 102-108 catch OSError/SubprocessError; lines 110-114 handle non-zero return; lines 116-122 handle unparseable output; lines 124-129 handle import_error.

claims.text: the candidate wins by an argument about import ordering, and nothing checks the argument still holds
claims.why: This module directly probes resolution rather than relying on import-order reasoning.

claims.text: Not necessarily fatal for the repo -- but it IS fatal for this evaluation
claims.why: The code returns ok=False with reason 'the candidate's interpreter cannot import daedalus', voiding the evaluation.

claims.text: __path__ is checked too: a namespace package has no __file__, and a candidate whose package dir lost its __init__.py would otherwise resolve to None and be read as 'no answer' rather than 'wrong tree'
claims.why: candidates includes both raw.get('daedalus_file') and raw.get('daedalus_path'), so a namespace package with __path__ inside the tree is accepted.

observations.what: The probe output format is not pinned beyond printing one JSON line; the code takes the last non-empty line and parses it, so a probe that prints extra output before the JSON would still work, but a probe that prints nothing yields raw={} and then fails with 'cannot import daedalus'? Actually raw.get('import_error') is None, resolved is None, candidates is empty, so it returns ok=False with 'resolves OUTSIDE' -- this is a silent 'absent' rather than 'unreadable' shape.

The probe inherits the environment, including PYTHONPATH, but the module does not sanitize it; the docstring warns that PYTHONPATH can break the mechanism, but the probe does not detect or mitigate it, so a misconfigured PYTHONPATH could still cause a false negative or positive.

check_import_provenance uses subprocess.run with check=False and captures stdout/stderr; the timeout_s default is 60 seconds, but no explicit kill is done beyond subprocess's own timeout handling, which is standard.

The resolved value reported in a successful ProvenanceCheck is raw.get('daedalus_file'), which may be None for a namespace package; the ok flag is True based on __path__ being under root, but the 'resolved' field would be None, potentially misleading callers who rely on it.

risks: line 116-140 | medium | Probe output format is not pinned; empty stdout yields raw={} and is reported as 'resolves OUTSIDE' rather than 'unreadable', which could mislead a caller into thinking a tree was resolved when it wasn't | Confirm whether a probe that prints nothing is expected to be treated as unreadable and adjust the error message accordingly

line 91-108 | medium | The probe inherits PYTHONPATH, the exact hazard named in the docstring, but the module does not detect or neutralize it; a PYTHONPATH that shadows daedalus could produce a false positive or false negative | Add an explicit check of os.environ.get('PYTHONPATH') in the probe or in check_import_provenance and report it

line 133-137 | low | A successful check may report resolved=None for a namespace package even though ok=True, which could confuse consumers of ProvenanceCheck.resolved | Test with a namespace package and decide whether resolved should fall back to the first __path__ entry
